Maintenance Report — MNT-0156-005

Asset: WELL-0156 (NE-08 Well 156, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 30 Jun 2023 08:00 · Finished: 30 Jun 2023 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0156-0037 on 2023-06-29 Report written: 01 Jul 2023

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0156-0037 at 14:15 on 2023-06-29 found crude oil on the pad: about 2.7% of the pad area, estimated 1.3 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.7 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 280 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 224 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 0.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0156-005 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.52% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0156-027

Asset: WELL-0156 (NE-08 Well 156, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 27 Jun 2026 08:00 · Finished: 01 Jul 2026 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 96 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward, Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0156-0190 on 2026-06-25 Report written: 01 Jul 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0156-0190 showed the wellhead at 33.1 °C with the air at 33.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 2 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.
